title: 2014 AMC 12B Problem 7
statement: For how many positive integers \(n\) is \(\dfrac{n}{30-n}\) also a positive integer?

solutions.text:
Write \[ \dfrac{n}{30-n} = \dfrac{30}{30-n} - 1. \]

For this to be a positive integer, \(30-n\) must be a positive divisor of \(30\) with \(\dfrac{30}{30-n} \ge 2,\) i.e. \(30-n \le 15.\)

The divisors of \(30\) that are at most \(15\) are \(1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15,\) giving \(7\) values of \(n\) (namely \(15, 20, 24, 25, 27, 28, 29\)).

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: So \(30-n\) must be a positive divisor of \(30,\) and the quotient must be at least \(2\)
